extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology (readers of a standard algebraic topology textbook)
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and exact criteria for computing and relating homotopy and homology groups of CW complexes and pairs (use of cellular approximation, connectivity hypotheses, Hurewicz theorem, plus construction, fibrations, and relative arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell‑attachment push‑off method for relative πi isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is obtained from C by attaching cells of certain dimensions and B is obtained from C by attaching cells of (other) dimensions, one proves surjectivity/injectivity of πi(A,C)→πi(X,B) by representing an element by a map f whose compact image meets finitely many cells and repeatedly pushing f off the cells of B−C one at a time (in order of decreasing dimension); injectivity uses the same idea applied to a homotopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the constructive method used in the Case analyses: represent classes by cellular maps with compact image, then remove intersections with attached cells using cellular approximation and inductive removal. The technique is applied cell-by-cell (decreasing dimension) and is the standard way to show maps on relative homotopy groups are surjective/injective when cells attached to A and B satisfy the stated dimension bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular approximation: high‑dimensional cells do not affect low πi
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher-dimensional cells have no effect on πi for i ≤ m+n (by cellular approximation); thus when proving statements about πi for small i one may replace a space by its skeleton up to a certain dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cellular approximation to ignore cells of dimension > relevant threshold (they can be discarded when computing πi up to that threshold). This simplifies inductive arguments on skeleta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑lemma / diagram chase criterion for isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative diagram of long exact sequences (e.g., triples (Ak,Ak−1,C) and (Xk,Xk−1,B)), if the corresponding adjacent vertical maps are isomorphisms (or surjective/injective appropriately) then the middle map is an isomorphism (or surjective) by the five‑lemma (or its one‑sided version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when you have exact sequences of triples and inductive hypotheses that give isomorphisms on other terms. Note: when i=2 some groups may be nonabelian and two right‑hand terms may not be groups, but the five‑lemma still applies with trivial modifications; for i=1 give a direct argument (often triviality or cellular approximation handles it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction by homotopy equivalence fixed on a subspace
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,C) and (B,C) satisfy connectivity assumptions then they are homotopy equivalent (via homotopy equivalences fixed on C) to pairs in a previously handled special case, so the general case reduces to that special case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 4.15 (CW approximation / homotopy equivalence arguments) to replace pairs by nicer models (with same C) and apply proved cases; homotopy equivalences fixed on C induce equivalences on unions A∪B.

rubrics_metrics.name: πn of a (finite) wedge/product of S^n (n ≥ 2) is free abelian on inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite wedge (or product under suitable connectivity hypotheses) of spheres S^n (n≥2), πn is free abelian with basis the homotopy classes of the inclusions of the summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are finitely many summands, cellular arguments and connectivity (e.g., pair being (2n−1) connected) give that inclusion of a summand induces an iso on πn. For infinitely many summands, use compactness of the image of a map S^n to reduce to a finite subwedge (direct limit argument).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute πn of S^1 ∨ S^n via universal cover and group‑ring module structure
rubrics_metrics.description: For n ≥ 2, πn(S^1 ∨ S^n) is a free Z[π1(S^1 ∨ S^n)]‑module on one generator (the inclusion of S^n); concretely πn(S^1 ∨ S^n) ≅ Z[t,t^−1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass to the universal cover (a copy of R with an S^n attached at each integer), compute πn there (free abelian on inclusions), and view lifts under π1 action to get the Z[π1]‑module structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.28: quotient map πi(X,A)→πi(X/A) is iso/surjective under connectivity bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X,A) is r‑connected and A is s‑connected with r,s ≥ 0, then the quotient map X→X/A induces an isomorphism πi(X,A)→πi(X/A) for i ≤ r+s and a surjection for i = r+s+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses attaching a cone on A (CA) and excision arguments: (CA,A) is (s+1)‑connected; apply long exact sequences and excision. Use when replacing a pair by a quotient simplifies computations of relative homotopy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realizing πn as quotient by attaching (n+1)-cells (Example 4.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is obtained from a wedge of S^n (n≥2) by attaching (n+1)-cells via basepoint‑preserving maps ϕβ, then πi(X)=0 for i<n and πn(X) is the quotient of the free abelian group πn(wedge) by the subgroup generated by the [ϕβ]; conversely every abelian group can be realized this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the long exact sequence of the pair (X, wedge) and identify the boundary map from πn+1(relative) with the subgroup generated by attaching maps. This is the standard method to construct spaces with prescribed πn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and uniqueness of K(G,n) (Eilenberg–MacLane spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW complex K(G,n) with only πn=G (abelian if n>1) can be built by making an (n−1)‑connected CW complex of dimension n+1 with πn≈G and then attaching higher‑dimensional cells to kill πi for i>n. The homotopy type of K(G,n) is uniquely determined by G and n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove uniqueness, construct map f inducing given isomorphism on πn (Lemma 4.31) and extend inductively over higher cells (since πn+1(K')=0, attaching maps extend). Use cellular approximation so attaching maps behave as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.31: extending maps determined by πn generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Given X built from S^n summands with (n+1)-cells attached and any ψ:πn(X)→πn(Y) with Y path‑connected, there exists f:X→Y with f_* = ψ; to extend over an (n+1)-cell one needs the composition of its attaching map with f to be nullhomotopic in Y (which holds because the attaching class is zero in πn(X)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct f on the n‑skeleton by mapping summand inclusions to representatives of ψ, then extend over (n+1)-cells since attaching maps are null in X. This is the standard extension criterion for building maps realizing a given homomorphism on πn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurewicz theorem (simple form) — link between first nonzero πn and Hn
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is (n−1)‑connected (n≥2) then Hi(X)=0 for i<n and πn(X) ≅ Hn(X). For a pair (X,A) that is (n−1)‑connected with A simply‑connected and nonempty, Hi(X,A)=0 for i<n and πn(X,A) ≅ Hn(X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to CW pairs, use Proposition 4.28 to turn relative case into absolute, throw away cells of dimension > n+1, identify πn(X) with cokernel of boundary map which equals cellular Hn; this is the primary tool to compute first nontrivial homotopy groups via homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 4.33: homology isomorphism implies homotopy equivalence (simply‑connected)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f:X→Y between simply‑connected CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence if f_*:Hn(X)→Hn(Y) is an isomorphism for each n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace f by inclusion via mapping cylinder, use relative Hurewicz theorem: vanishing Hn(Y,X) implies vanishing πn(Y,X), hence isomorphisms on all πn and homotopy equivalence. Useful as a practical criterion: check homology isomorphisms to establish equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example 4.35 caution: nontrivial π1‑action can break πn vs Hn correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist spaces (e.g., X=(S^1∨S^n)∪e^{n+1} with attaching map corresponding to 2t−1) where inclusion S^1→X induces iso on all homology and πi for i<n but not on πn, due to nontrivial π1 action on πn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This warns that Hurewicz/Whitehead type criteria require hypotheses (simply‑connected or trivial π1 action); nontrivial π1 action can produce torsion/quotients in πn invisible to homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurewicz map and its algebraic properties (Proposition 4.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hurewicz map h:πn(X,A,x0)→Hn(X,A) (n>0) is defined by h([f])=f_*(α) and is a homomorphism when n>1 (absolute h for n≥1 is similarly a homomorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses decomposition (f+g)_* = f_* + g_* via collapsing equator map D^n→D^n∨D^n. Use this to relate group operation in πn to sum in homology; keep track of basepoint issues in relative case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor out π1‑action to get π'_n for general relative Hurewicz (definition and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: When π1 acts nontrivially on πn(X,A), define π'_n(X,A,x0) as the quotient of πn by the subgroup generated by elements of the form [γ][f]−[f]; the Hurewicz map descends to h':π'_n→Hn, and the general Hurewicz theorem asserts h' is iso under connectivity hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quotient removes basepoint‑change ambiguity coming from π1(A) action; necessary for the relative Hurewicz theorem (Theorem 4.37) when A is not simply‑connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.37 (general relative Hurewicz)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X,A) is an (n−1)‑connected pair of path‑connected spaces with n≥2 and A≠∅, then h':π'_n(X,A,x0)→Hn(X,A) is an isomorphism and Hi(X,A)=0 for i<n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: arrange CW pair with cells of X−A of dimension ≥ n, reduce to X=X^{n+1}, compare cellular boundary map with relative π groups using Lemma 4.38 and five‑lemma style diagram chase. For n=2 additional arguments show π'_2 is abelian and h' is iso.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.38: relative πn of an attachment is a free π1(X)‑module
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is connected and W is obtained by attaching n‑cells e^n_α (n≥2) to X, and if inclusion π1(X)→π1(W) is an isomorphism, then πn(W,X) is a free π1(X)‑module with basis the homotopy classes of the characteristic maps of the n‑cells. For n=2, π2(W,X) is generated by the characteristic maps together with their images under π1 action (and more structure exists when π1 map is not iso).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When π1 inclusion is iso, analyze universal cover: lifts of attached n‑cells under deck transformations give basis; when n=2 and π1 not iso, one must use Whitehead's theory of free crossed modules. Apply this lemma to identify generators of relative π in cellular arguments for Hurewicz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.39: relation in π2 and abelianization of π'_2
rubrics_metrics.description: For any (X,A,x0) the identity a + b − a = (∂a)b holds for all a,b ∈ π2(X,A,x0), where ∂:π2→π1 is the boundary; hence after quotienting by elements [γ][f]−[f] (i.e., passing to π'_2) the group becomes abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic relation shows how conjugation by boundary elements twists the nonabelian π2; quotienting kills the twisting and yields an abelian group suitable for the Hurewicz isomorphism at n=2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plus construction (Proposition 4.40): killing perfect subgroups while preserving homology
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a connected CW complex with H1(X)=0 (π1 perfect) then there exists a simply‑connected CW complex X^+ and a map X→X^+ inducing isomorphisms on all homology groups. More generally one may kill a perfect subgroup H⊂π1(X) and produce X^+ with induced map π1(X)→π1(X^+) surjective with kernel the normal subgroup generated by H, while preserving homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: attach 2‑cells along loops generating π1 to kill π1, then split H2 and attach 3‑cells representing the free summand to kill unwanted π2 while preserving homology. Known as Quillen plus construction; useful to simplify π1 without changing homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibration criterion: homotopy lifting property (Serre fibration) and long exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: If p:E→B has the homotopy lifting property with respect to disks D^k for all k≥0 (equivalently for all CW pairs), then p_*:πn(E,F,x0)→πn(B,b0) is an isomorphism for all n≥1, and if B is path‑connected there is a long exact sequence ···→πn(F)→πn(E)→πn(B)→πn−1(F)→···→π0(E)→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relative homotopy lifting to lift maps In→B to E starting from J^{n−1} and extend cell-by-cell; this gives surjectivity and injectivity of p_* as needed. Such maps are often called Serre fibrations and are the setting for homotopy exact sequences of fiber bundles (examples: projection of product, Hopf fibration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy lifting property equivalence and practical lifting method
rubrics_metrics.description: The homotopy lifting property for disks is equivalent to the lifting property for all CW pairs because lifts can be constructed inductively over skeleta: extending a lift over one cell reduces to the disk case by composing with the characteristic map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checking a map is a Serre fibration, it suffices to verify the lifting property on disks. In proofs of long exact sequences of fibrations, construct lifts over J^{n−1} and extend to In via the relative lifting property.
